claude-settings.title: Claude Code: Settings (where settings live, precedence)

claude-mcp.title: Claude Code: MCP (scopes, project server approvals and workspace trust)

codex-permissions-source.title: openai/codex: codex-rs/protocol/src/permissions.rs (read-only and workspace-write policies start from :root = Read)

claude.read_inside.text: File reads need no approval within the working directory and additional directories; outside them, Manual mode asks.

claude.readonly_commands.text: Read-only Bash commands such as cat, head, tail, grep and find run without a permission prompt in every mode, except as blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories changes for paths outside the working directories.

claude.deny_scope.text: Read and Edit deny rules apply to the built-in file tools, to file commands Claude Code recognises in Bash (cat, head, tail, sed, tee) and to redirection targets. They don't apply to a command that reads files without naming them, or to arbitrary subprocesses that read files indirectly, like a Python or Node script that opens files itself.

claude.precedence.text: Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow; the first match in that order decides, and specificity doesn't change it.

claude.anchors.text: //path is absolute, ~/path is under home, /path is relative to the settings source (the primary working directory for project and local settings, ~/.claude for user settings), and path or ./path is relative to the current directory; bare names match at any depth.

claude.modes.text: Permission modes: default (Manual), acceptEdits, plan, auto (a classifier reviews actions), dontAsk (denies what would prompt), bypassPermissions (skips prompts).

claude.block_reads_outside.text: permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories makes the file tools refuse reads outside the working directories in every permission mode.

claude.sandbox_off.text: The sandbox is off by default; it runs on macOS (Seatbelt), Linux and WSL2 (bubblewrap). On native Windows, commands run unsandboxed.

claude.sandbox_reads.text: The sandbox allows reading most of the machine, including credential files such as ~/.ssh and ~/.aws/credentials, unless denyRead or Read deny rules say otherwise; the two are merged.

claude.sandbox_outside.text: Built-in file and web tools follow permission rules, not the sandbox; hooks, local MCP servers and helper commands such as apiKeyHelper run with your full access.

claude.sandbox_auto_allow.text: autoAllowBashIfSandboxed defaults to true: sandboxed Bash commands run without a prompt.

claude.sandbox_escape.text: Commands in excludedCommands run outside the sandbox, and Claude can ask to retry a failed command unsandboxed unless allowUnsandboxedCommands is false.

claude.sandbox_unavailable.text: When the platform doesn't support the sandbox or its dependency check fails, Claude Code runs commands without sandboxing unless sandbox.failIfUnavailable is true.

claude.sandbox_network.text: Sandboxed commands reach the network only through a proxy that checks each host against allowedDomains, which start empty.

claude.trust.text: Project allow rules and additional directories wait for workspace trust; deny and ask rules apply at once.

claude.mcp_scopes.text: MCP servers come from ~/.claude.json (user and local scope), the project's .mcp.json (approved per server or with enableAllProjectMcpServers) and managed-mcp.json.

codex.modes.text: sandbox_mode is read-only, workspace-write or danger-full-access; workspace-write is the default low-friction mode for local work.

codex.approvals.text: approval_policy is on-request (work inside the sandbox, ask to go beyond it) or never; untrusted is unsupported and on-failure deprecated.

codex.reads.text: The read-only and workspace-write policies start from read access to the filesystem root: sandboxed commands can read the whole disk unless a permissions profile denies paths.

codex.network.text: sandbox_workspace_write.network_access allows outbound network access inside the workspace-write sandbox.

codex.env.text: shell_environment_policy.ignore_default_excludes keeps variables containing KEY, SECRET or TOKEN (default: true); set to false to exclude them.

codex.deny.text: A [permissions.<name>] profile can deny reads of paths and globs such as **/*.env with "deny".

codex.trust.text: A project-local .codex/config.toml applies only to trusted projects (projects.<path>.trust_level).

codex.platforms.text: macOS uses Seatbelt, Linux and WSL2 need bubblewrap, native Windows has its own sandbox in PowerShell.
